turns.text: Hey Lloyd, can you help me draft a follow-up email to Daniel? I want to suggest he try out the new open-source model we looked at last week instead of sticking with the current API provider.

Sure, Alan. Here is a draft: 'Hi Daniel, hope you're well. Given the recent performance metrics, I suggest we test the new open-source model to see if it fits your workflow better. Let me know what you think.' Shall I send it?

No, wait. Delete that. You don't get Daniel. He observes that leading compounds in AI, noting users migrate to the best model and stay there. He won't waste time on 'testing' something unless it's already the top performer. He only switches when the new thing is objectively better than what he has.

Understood. I will adjust the tone to reflect that he only adopts top-tier solutions directly, rather than experimenting. Here is a revised draft: 'Hi Daniel, the new model has outperformed our current provider in benchmarks. Since you only switch when there is a clear upgrade, I thought this might be worth a look.'
Better. But make it shorter. He hates fluff. Just get to the point about it being the best.
How about this: 'Hi Daniel, the new model is currently the top performer in benchmarks. Given your preference for only switching to the best option, I thought you'd want to know. Best, Alan.'
Perfect. Send that. Also, did the printer get fixed? My toner is empty.
Email sent. Regarding the printer, I have scheduled a maintenance check for tomorrow morning at 9 AM. You can keep using your laptop for now.
